rows.sourceText: **What the number means.** These cascade files are the CSS glass-ui publishes in its package and a consumer's bundler resolves through the single `@import "@mkbabb/glass-ui/styles"`. Most of the weight ships to the browser verbatim — the `@theme` custom properties (tokens.css), and all the plain CSS rules (`.glass-*`, `.dock-*`, the SFC scoped CSS). The `@utility`/`@apply` arm (utilities.css) is the one part the consumer's Tailwind tree-shakes, so gating its full source is a conservative over-count — acceptable for a package-weight gate, and the part the W4 consolidation (D6) most reduces. rows.sourceText: **Constellation (G.W2 → AV.W8).** Slides `constellation.ts` hand-rolls the RAF triplet (`anyActive`/`ensureRunning`/`frame`, lines 448-461), a MutationObserver state-cache (463-476), per-frame PRM check (393), and O(n²) brute-force neighbor query (240-247). G.W2 swaps the RAF/visibility machinery for `useRAFLoop` + `useIntersectionPause`, extracts `drawAnomaly(ctx, node, phase, k)` as a slides-local method, and preserves the static-frame path under `?freeze`/PRM. This makes slides the 2nd resolving consumer that unblocks AV.W8 (`useCanvas2D` + Constellation primitive). AV.W8 lands the generic lattice (proximity-graph + spatial-binning O(n) + optional Verlet settle) with D2 draw discipline (no shadowBlur — pre-rendered glow sprite, polyline batching per opacity bucket, floored coords, never getImageData). The slides red ANOMALY skin is a consumer overlay (FOLD-G extract), never baked into the primitive. AV.W8 is ADOPT-gated: lands at ≥2 resolving consumers (demo story + G.W2 swap), else GATED-NOT-LANDED with G.W2 named as the trigger.

rows.sourceText: **1. SDF shape morph = mix two distance fields by a `morphFactor`.** The canonical technique: compute `d1 = sdShapeA(p)`, `d2 = sdShapeB(p)`, then `d = mix(d1, d2, morphFactor)` — at 0 you see A, at 1 you see B, intermediate values are a true in-between form. Drive `morphFactor` with an eased clock for smooth metamorphosis. ([den4ic, DEV Community](https://dev.to/den4ic/morphing-geometric-shapes-with-sdf-in-glsl-fragment-shaders-and-visualization-in-jetpack-compose-5db8); [roombawulf/sdf-morph](https://github.com/roombawulf/sdf-morph)). Color/glow accents in the same idiom: `col *= 1.05 - exp(-6.0*abs(d))` (edge fade) and `col *= 0.8 + 0.2*cos(110.0*d)` (interior bands) ([den4ic, Medium](https://medium.com/@den4icccccc/morphing-geometric-shapes-with-sdf-in-glsl-fragment-shaders-and-visualization-in-jetpack-compose-48fd8d403e24)).

rows.sourceText: **Caveat (load-bearing):** `mix(d1, d2, t)` of two SDFs is a *pseudo*-SDF, not a Euclidean distance field — sign is preserved but magnitude is wrong. This is fine for a 2D fill mask with `fwidth`-based AA (what GooBlob already does at `metaball.frag.ts:149`), but it would break anything relying on exact distance (true outline thickness, raymarch step safety). For GooBlob's fill-and-AA pipeline it is safe. ([Ronja's 2D SDF Combination](https://www.ronja-tutorials.com/post/035-2d-sdf-combination/); [Higher-Order Algebraic SDFs, CAD Journal 2023](https://cad-journal.net/files/vol_20/CAD_20(5)_2023_1005-1028.pdf)).

rows.sourceText: **4. Premium metaball interaction = a pointer *trail* of shrinking spheres, not one push.** Codrops' June 2025 droplet-metaballs keeps an array of ~15 historical pointer positions and places spheres along it with decreasing radius (`radius - baseRadius*fi`), producing an elastic, stretchy follow. Their merge uses the **exponential** smin `-log(exp(-k*d1)+exp(-k*d2))/k` with `k=7.0`. They also use 3D value noise on the reflection vector for surface life. ([Codrops — Interactive Droplet-like Metaballs with Three.js and GLSL, 2025-06-09](https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/06/09/how-to-create-interactive-droplet-like-metaballs-with-three-js-and-glsl/)). GooBlob's satellites are already a sphere pool — a trail is the same primitive driven by pointer history instead of orbit math.

rows.sourceText: - **`renderMode.ts` — the ASYNC probe.** The current `resolveRenderMode` is SYNCHRONOUS, returning `"webgl"|"css"` (`renderMode.ts:31`). Add `resolveRenderModeAsync` returning `"webgpu"|"webgl"|"css"`: `await navigator.gpu?.requestAdapter({powerPreference:"high-performance"})` — `requestAdapter` NEVER rejects (resolves `null` when unsupported), so guard the null AND check `!adapter.isFallbackAdapter` (a software/fallback adapter drops to `"webgl"`, NOT `"webgpu"` — a software impl is slower than the WebGL2 fragment path). The async probe runs behind the SAME deferred idle-tick arm the WebGL path uses; the CSS placeholder paints FIRST so the probe cannot block first paint (this touches `Aurora.vue`'s first-paint ordering — the reason W7b is its own rung). The synchronous `resolveRenderMode` STAYS for the existing low-power-tier `"auto"` resolution; the async form is additive.

The `measure` mode option I first added was a FALSE distinction (both topologies are identical) and was removed — the one deferred path serves both, so the inner call site needs no thread.

rows.sourceText: **Collapse (expanded→collapsed)** is the mirror: `fromSize = getSize(.dock-layers) = ~195` (the `.expanded:not([data-morphing])` `width:100%` box content), the rAF measures `toSize = ~40` (post-flush, `--summary` now in-flow, `--full` absolute-stretched), the spring runs 195→40. CRITICAL: this is why the deferred post-flush measurement is REQUIRED and a synchronous `scrollWidth` of the inactive target pane would NOT work — collapsing, the target `--summary` is the absolute/`inset:0`-STRETCHED pane (~195px box, centered icon, no overflow), so its `scrollWidth` reads ~195 (the stretched box), not its ~40 natural; only measuring it AFTER it becomes the in-flow shrink-wrap pane yields the correct ~40.

The 'reaches medium parity' re-enable criterion is therefore never actually met by the wave chain — WebGPU would paint a smooth+Kuwahara field that still diverges from WebGL2's per-pixel oil/pastel/vangogh stroke SDFs.

(A)+(B) eliminate the visible pop; (C) is the structural hysteresis the listener-on-morphing-root design currently lacks.

The mechanism (re-grepped at HEAD, CONFIRMED by the value.js N2 fleet on a live 3.13.0 registry consumer): `dockMorphContext.ts:271-361` `onSwap` — the pin (`:316-319`) + the ONE-rAF measure-defer (`:344-360`) that forces `inline-size:max-content` on the OUTER `.dock-layers` for the single measurement. A nested `<DockLayerGroup>` registers a SECOND morph target via `morphHost.registerGroup({containerEl, activeLayer, axis})` (`DockLayerGroup.vue:92-93`); during the outer FLIP's measure window the active full pane's ONLY content is the nested `.dock-layer-stack` — itself a pinned morph target STILL at its collapsed span in the SAME rAF — so the outer measure shrink-wraps to ~0. Replicating the measure on a SETTLED-expanded dock reads the correct 261.1px → the bug is measurement ORDERING, not geometry. The value.js live trace (`U-DOCK.md §1`): from a rested-collapsed state `expand()` arms `from:40px → to:0px`, the box springs the WRONG direction (55→19px over ~200ms), dead-holds at 19px for ~455ms, then SNAPS 19→280px in one un-animated frame; the four-cycle probe reads `to:0px` every cycle. The `AY.W-GOD1 §F2` booking (`dockMorphContext.ts:328-343`) under-scopes this as "first-mount intermittent / interaction-order-dependent" — it tested a NON-nested `#persistent` slider dock (`data-testid="dock-capture"`, `:341-343`); this RE-SCOPES it to deterministic-for-any-nested-group with the value.js four-cycle reproduction (`U-DOCK.md §5` recipe 2). **THE FENCE (the letter is explicit, do NOT cross it): the spring constants are FINE — `DOCK_SPRING {response:0.32, dampingFraction:0.7}` (`constants.ts:32`) — this is NOT a clock/spring defect, the fix is a measure-ORDERING change in `onSwap`, never a timing re-tune.**

rows.sourceText: **(a) The reading-order inversion on the hero pages — the page describes a thing before naming it (A4 finding 2, HIGH).** `StoryPage.vue:46-68` renders the chrome `<header>` (the mono eyebrow `text-admin-label` `:47` + the dense blurb `text-small text-muted-foreground` `:65`) and SUPPRESSES the chrome `<h1>` on `variant==='page'` (`:62` guard, the D1-4 double-`<h1>` fix) — but on the 10 hero rows (`manifest.ts hero:true`) `StoryHero.vue:252,280` renders a huge `text-display-3` `<h1>` (clamp peak 67.8px / 600) INSIDE the card, BELOW that header. So the eyebrow + a 3-5 line blurb sit in the top chrome band, THEN the giant title appears beneath. Captured (glass-material / GooBlob / Fourier-Studio / aurora desktop): "UNIFIED MATERIAL…" eyebrow + the dense paragraph FIRST, "Glass Material" display title SECOND — a focal inversion (the descriptor before the name) AND two focal points stacked in the already-crowded top band (the same band the dock chips graze — finding (c)). iOS-26 frames hierarchy as the FIRST design pillar: a left-aligned title/subtitle stack in reading order, **never subtitle-above-title** (createwithswift). The fix: ONE coherent ordered cluster — eyebrow → display `<h1>` → blurb, top-to-bottom — never split across the chrome/card boundary, the blurb a clearly subordinate rung UNDER the title, the descriptor shown ONCE.

rows.sourceText: - **The ASYNC device-acquisition prelude (`armAsync()`).** `createCanvasLifecycle.arm()` is synchronous; the WebGPU device request is a Promise. The wrapper owns the async PRELUDE: `armAsync()` awaits `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()` → `adapter.requestDevice()`, configures the context (`canvas.getContext("webgpu")` → `context.configure({ device, format: navigator.gpu.getPreferredCanvasFormat(), alphaMode: "premultiplied" })`), runs the consumer's `setup(device, context, format) → WebGPUCanvasFrame`, THEN calls the leaf's synchronous `arm()`. The leaf stays untouched (paralleling how `useCanvas2D` owns its Vue `toValue`/`onScopeDispose` deferred-arm prelude). `buildContext()` returns the leaf's `CanvasFrameHooks` synchronously off the already-resolved device; `frame(t)` records a command encoder, begins a render pass against the current swap-chain texture view (`context.getCurrentTexture().createView()`), draws, and submits. `shouldContinue`/`time?`/`teardown` mirror the WebGL backend exactly. **If the device-acquire shape genuinely cannot thread through the existing leaf seam WITHOUT a leaf public-seam change, that is a recorded Triumvirate (a leaf seam ADD the other two backends ignore), NOT a fork** (§3a).

rows.sourceText: **Finding:** AURORA IS DEAD ON A REAL GPU. On the live demo (:5199, /substrates/aurora, this M5 Max — ANGLE Metal, navigator.gpu PRESENT) the aurora renders NOTHING procedural: the visible "aurora" is 100% a static CSS `.aurora-placeholder linear-gradient(135deg, blue→cream)` band, and the WebGPU canvas stacked over it paints ZERO pixels. LIVE PROOF: the `aurora-canvas--armed` class is set, `getContext("webgpu")` is bound, the render loop runs — yet compositing the canvas over white deviated 0 of 20,712 sampled pixels from pure white (the swapchain is fully blank/transparent); composited raw, alpha=0 at every sample incl. dead-center over a nucleus. So `useGpuSubstrate` picks the WebGPU backend (`supportsWebGPU() && setupWGPU != null`), the WGSL `aurora.wgsl` pipeline arms, draws every frame, and emits an empty surface — the static blue gradient shows through. ROOT CAUSE = the W-AURORA-WGPU "parity verified" close is a gestalt-bar evasion: the WGSL primary path was NEVER run on a real GPU before being flipped `aurora:verified`. The DELTA's own words: "Measured: mean ΔE = 0.0" is a DEVICE-FREE STRUCTURAL PROXY — it transcribed both shaders' COLOR MATH into JS and diffed the two JS functions; "The BINDING Metal-GPU live capture-pair … rides W-REFLECT3" — the actual GPU render check was DEFERRED to a reflection wave that never ran. The committed proof PNG `aurora-wgpu-primary.png` IS the broken state: a 96×96 flat blue→cream gradient (the CPU color-seam swatch / the placeholder), not a rendered procedural field, rubber-stamped as the primary capture. SECOND failure: ALL FIVE preset thumbnails are dead — console: "[Aurora] thumbnail bake aborted: Error: [useWebGPUCanvas] device not acquired" — the `capture`/`eager` bake path calls the SYNC `arm()` (→ `buildContext` → `throw "device not acquired"`) because only `armAsync` awaits the async WebGPU device; capture mode was never wired through `armAsync`. THIRD: the van-Gogh / oil-pastel / oil-modes / kuwahara / watercolor / pastel / crayon mediums DO NOT EXIST on the WebGPU primary — `aurora.wgsl.ts:320` admits "The painterly mediums (uMedium 1-6) are the WebGL2 fallback's register; the WGSL primary renders the smooth core … (the booked W-AURORA-WGPU-MEDIUMS successor ports the painterly bodies)." So even when WGSL eventually paints, a watercolor/vangogh preset (Meadow/Day9/Deliberative — the SHIPPED defaults) can only ever render the smooth core; the painterly corpus (vangogh-medium.glsl.ts, oil-modes.glsl.ts, mediums.glsl.ts) is GLSL-only and unreachable on the primary backend a modern browser selects. FOURTH: the W-AURORA-SWRASTER "luminance-faithful fallback ground" (`auroraFallbackGround`) only engages when `resolvedRenderMode === "css"` (Aurora.vue:150-159); a capable GPU resolves `"webgl"`, so the user gets the OLD flat `paletteToCssGradient` band the swraster wave claimed to retire — the field-faithful ground never ships to a real user. NET: aurora is non-functional + non-interactive on every WebGPU-capable browser (the majority — Chrome/Edge/Safari-26 on Apple Silicon); the "WebGPU-first procedural-viz suite, Batch V COMPLETE" is unimplemented paint behind green CPU-proxy gates.

rows.sourceText: **Gestalt direction:** RIP OUT the deferred-π model entirely — it is the disease. The "binding π LOCAL-ONLY rides W-REFLECT3" pattern let 52 waves close "complete" on source-green while ONE downstream wave owned ALL paint truth, and that wave never ran. BC must INVERT this: NO wave closes without its OWN fresh both-mode capture against :5199 INLINE (the gestalt verdict is a PRECONDITION of the wave's close, not a deferred batch). Kill W-REFLECT3-as-a-single-gate; make proof:ba-gestalt's freshness-hash a per-wave born-RED that cannot be deferred. (1) FOLD the unexecuted BB Batches 5/6/7 wholesale into BC but RE-VERIFY their paint first — do not trust the SPEC, re-ground each on the live demo (W-DECK/W-SLIDES-DRIVE/W-ADOPT/W-CONSUMER-MODERNIZE are cross-repo and gated on a CORRECT glass-ui, which does not exist yet — they sequence AFTER the glass-rebuild, not before). (3) The 178-commit dock + the white-morph + the wrong-rail are a SINGLE ground-up rebuild (the dock as the "epigrammatic exemplar of motion+glass") — fold the chronic dock register (W-DOCK-MORPH-FAMILY/W-DOCK-GEOMETRY/W-RAIL3/W-DOCK-SECTIONS/W-CHIP-GRAZE/the 178 commits) into ONE BC dock-rebuild that subsumes them, plus the NEW asks (macOS expanded-stack rail, arbitrary-shape liquid morph, the always-on metaball-teardrop now un-booked from its perf-gate since the morph IS the headline). rows.sourceText: - **D9' root (the BLACK VOID on the user's real Chrome): `renderMode:"auto"` collapses to a STATIC "css" placeholder.** `Aurora.vue:106` resolves `resolveRenderMode("auto", ...)`, and `renderMode.ts:121-160` returns `"css"` (the static `paletteToCssGradient`/`auroraFallbackGround` placeholder, NO WebGL arm — `useAurora.ts:256` `if (cssOnly) return`) when ANY low-power signal is present: **`navigator.hardwareConcurrency <= 4`** (line 146-147) OR `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` OR `connection.saveData`. On a user Chrome with ≤4 logical cores (or a throttled/battery-saver session), aurora renders a STATIC gradient and never animates — the "renders SLOW / dark dead cards" the user reports. The `"css"` placeholder is a flat `linear-gradient(135deg, …)` whose mean luminance can diverge from the real composite. This is a real, common-host downgrade, NOT a true crash — but it reads as broken.

rows.sourceText: - **D7 (Safari `fwidth` + context-loss flash): the two derivative sites.** `metaball.frag.ts:266` (`float aa = max(fwidth(d), 1e-6)` — the AA-edge half-width) + `:364` (`float nVar = length(fwidth(N))` — the Toksvig normal-variance spec-clamp) are the "most rasterizer-drift-prone lines." Both are mirrored to WGSL (`metaball.wgsl.ts:397, 450`). WebKit is stricter about `precision highp float` derivatives + context-loss churn (the "rapidly FLASHES" = WebGL context lost + re-arm storm). Fix: prefer the WebGPU primary on Safari 26 (Metal — no `fwidth`-derivative variance), explicit `precision highp float` (present), a robust `webglcontextlost`/`restored` lifecycle that re-arms ONCE not a churn loop. The analytic-gradient normal (no 4-tap) already reduces derivative sensitivity — keep it.

rows.sourceText: **The "first main page" rule (which D2-vs-D3 a story gets, made deterministic):** within each category's `stories[]` array (`manifest.ts:CATEGORIES`), the FIRST story is the D2 MAIN (the marquee anchor — e.g. substrates→aurora, forms→inputs, display→buttons, containers→dialog); every subsequent story is a D3 SUB-page. The `s()` factory cannot infer "is-first" cross-category, so the depth is the EXPLICIT `heroScale` cell per row (the table assigns D2 to the first/marquee story, D3 `4` to the rest). A category whose first story is a live-GL marquee (substrates) holds `hero` on the main; a calm-band first story (forms/inputs) holds `5` for the main and `4` for the subs — the depth step is preserved within the band's GL budget.

The router already resolves a category id (`manifest.ts:byCategory`); the section-landing is the category's index view (the front-door redirect-card grid GENERALIZED to a per-section landing — NOT a new component, the SAME `StoryHero` chassis at `heroScale: hero` + the bento grid). An `error`-severity message on ANY assembled WGSL string REDs (born-RED on the planted `var target`). The per-viz waves keep their shader BODIES; this wave owns the cross-cutting COMPILE assert over all of them. rows.sourceText: - **(under-shadow soften, §1.1/2.b)** — softening `--glass-btn-under-shadow` quiet→wash REDUCES the depth drop. The doc argues the bright inset-top specular COMPENSATES (depth via highlight, not drop). That is the correct iOS-27 model (inner light, not inner dark). But it is a TRADE — less grounding shadow for more top highlight. If the compensating specular is not composed in the SAME wave, the button reads FLATTER (thinner glass) for a window. **D6 holds only if (rim) + (under-shadow soften) + (specular compose) land TOGETHER, never partially.** The wave must be atomic.

rows.sourceText: **BUT "append-at-end so existing offsets are byte-stable" (§4, §9) is imprecise.** The WGPU struct (`uniformBridgeWGPU.ts:10-27`) has EXISTING PAD LANES: `scalars3.w` (off 60, currently `0`), `ints1.y/z/w` (off 100/104/108), `nuc2.y/z/w`, `kuwahara.z/w` (off 568/572). 5 scalars could fit into existing pad slots (`scalars3.w` + a new `scalars6` vec4 = 4 lanes, with 1 spilling) WITHOUT growing the 576-byte buffer if packed into pads — OR appending a clean `scalars6: vec4` (4 lanes) + 1 spilling into a pad. The spec says "append at end" which is SAFE (576→592) but the claim "byte-stable offsets" is only true for the PRE-EXISTING lanes; the spec does not specify whether the 5 metal scalars pack into 2 new vec4s (8 lanes, 3 wasted) or scavenge pads (alignment-fragile). **A reviewer must force the exact lane assignment** — a careless metal-uniform pack that reorders or mis-aligns is exactly the std140-vs-WGSL garbage-read trap `uniformBridgeWGPU.ts`'s whole header warns against. "Bounded" ✓; "byte-stable" needs the explicit lane map the spec defers.

rows.sourceText: **The delta:** "Edges on left and right aren't quite as dark grey." The perimeter ink is ALREADY a whisper (≤5%, BC.W-BLACK-BAR), so the residual L/R darkness is NOT the border ink — it is the omnidirectional component of the under-shadow / the lack of a SIDE catch. The directional rim (D3) carries TOP+BOTTOM; the L/R edges currently get only the faint perimeter ink. The fix: confirm the L/R edges read the same lit-glass register (a faint side catch OR simply the perimeter ink staying ≤5% with no added side darkening), so the four edges read as a continuous lit rim, not dark-grey sides framing lit top/bottom. This is largely VERIFIED-already (BC.W-BLACK-BAR did the work); the audit confirms the L/R darkness is gone and the directional rim (D3) completes the four-edge lit read. **Mostly a re-affirm + a π readback, not a new token.**

rows.sourceText: - **Is the base-`<Card>` hover-deadness a SRC gap or a DEMO gap?** The component report frames A1 as a potential **src** finding — "a default `<Card>` is animation-DEAD … the library SHIPS the entrance vocabulary but Card consumes none of it" — and floats a NEW `BD.W-CARD-AFFORDANCE` src wave (default-on hover-lift for content cards). The design report frames the SAME observation as a **demo** gap (opt the *specimens* into `:pressable` + `v-specular`). **Resolution: this is DEMO-side for this page, with a NARROW src question deferred.** The card page's job is to SHOW the four-state contract by opting specimens into the already-shipped `:pressable`/`specular`/cartoon-lift axes — zero src paint needed to fix the page. Whether a *bare* content `<Card>` should ship a default-on hover-lift is a real but SEPARATE library-identity decision (it risks animating every static content plate library-wide, a regression surface) — it does NOT block this page and should NOT be minted as a card-page action. Book it as a question to the affordance-map owner, do not mint a src wave off one page.

rows.sourceText: - **The pane-swap is ONE spring, ONE scalar, transparently nested.** A `<DockLayerGroup>` inside a `<GlassDock>` DEFERS its pane-swap to the dock's single orchestrator via `registerGroup` (`dockMorphContext.ts:466`) — it registers as a SECOND morph target on the dock's ONE `SpringProgress`/`--dock-morph-t` clock, so a simultaneous collapse + pane-swap is co-driven with no second engine. rows.sourceText: - **The real blob↔meatball / dot↔dot metaball transition** (the goo-blob + worm already do this): the SDF `smin` (smooth-minimum / polynomial smooth-union) field. Two distance fields blended by `smin(d1, d2, k)` produce a NECK that wells up + pinches off as the shapes approach/separate — the "metaball merge". This is exactly what `metaball.frag`'s `sceneDistG` does (satellites smin'd into the body) and what the SVG goo filter (`feGaussianBlur` → `feColorMatrix` alpha-threshold) approximates in 2D for the worm/fission bridge. The blob↔meatball morph the user wants is therefore: keep the SAME smin field (geometry identical), and lerp the SURFACE (lit/shadow) on a `uMorphT` scalar — a shading morph over a shared metaball field, NOT a path interpolation.

rows.sourceText: **The one genuine judgement call (recorded, not blocking):** the AA arm asserts contrast over the field-ADJACENT smooth patch, not the literal sub-glyph pixels (unreadable under opaque ink). This is the `pixel-analysis.mjs` discipline and is correct where the field is low-frequency near text (the recessive calm field is — C≤0.046, smooth by the DELTA's own measurement). On a HIGH-frequency field behind text (a focal vivid hero, the `/substrates/aurora` studio case) the adjacent patch is a weaker proxy — the DELTA itself notes the focal-hero pixel ratios are "offset-patch artifacts over a spatially-varying vivid field." So the AA arm's roster is the RECESSIVE-field surfaces (the legibility floor case, where the field is calm-by-design); the focal vivid heroes are gestalt-judged by `proof:ba-gestalt`, NOT this arm (the field there is the page's SUBJECT, vivid is correct, and the contrast is a placement judgement not a band). Recording this scope keeps the arm honest — it asserts where the measurement is valid, and defers the spatially-varying case to the human gestalt verdict.

rows.sourceText: | F2.5 | BG.W-GLASS-DEPTH-TIER (SOTA-DESIGN [8] — thickness by prominence) | F2 | P | DONE `(paint-pass)` — **[JUDGED-PASS 2026-07-05, dual-engine Chrome/ANGLE-Metal + WebKit/Metal, both modes]** the freeze-fix PAINTS: the tier ladder is strictly-increasing content 14.05px < popover 15.1px < menu 16px (both blur AND saturate, both engines, both modes, byte-identical), the live `primary-audacious` CTA on `/display/buttons` resolves `--glass-depth: 0.35` and paints backdrop-filter blur **14.05px** (was the frozen 16px menu-ceiling in the prior FAIL) — thickness-by-prominence is REAL, the dead-knob CLOSED. Fences HELD: calm content default byte-unchanged (non-deep ladder wash 1/quiet 8/resting 8/floating 13/overlay 20/card 8), one-deep-refractive-per-route (`.glass-deep` count buttons 1/popover 0/dropdown 0, lens 0, main.children 2), no `--glass-blur-*` re-pointed by the tier map. All 12 capture PNGs resolve on disk at 2880×1800 with per-engine in-pixel provenance badges (`docs/tranches/BG/audit/visual/pipeline-depth-tier/`); DELTA `docs/tranches/BG/audit/visual/BG.W-GLASS-DEPTH-TIER-DELTA.md`. **Prior FREEZE-FIX INTEGRATED on `tranche/BG`:** the deep LERP (`--glass-blur-deep-active-radius` / `--glass-saturate-deep-active` / `--glass-blur-deep`) MOVED from `:root` (`tokens/glass-deep.css`) to the CONSUMING `.glass-deep` rule (`glass/deep.css`), so `var(--glass-depth)` — a REGISTERED `@property` (`inherits:true; initial-value:1`) CSS eager-substitutes at its DECLARING element — now resolves to the element's LIVE tier grade instead of freezing at the `:root` initial-value 1. The tier map sets `--glass-depth` per band on the base rung the `.glass-deep` decoration composes with; the LERP now PAINTS the ladder content ~14px < popover ~15px < menu 16px (the C18 dual-engine painted dead-knob closed). ENDPOINTS + GRADES stay at `:root` (literals — no registered-`@property` read, safe); the COMPOSITION moved to the consuming element only. `proof:glass` GREEN on the integrated tree incl. the EXTENDED depth-tier arm — DT4 freeze-guard `lerp-at=.glass-deep per-element=✓ ladder=14.05px < 15.10px < 16.00px` (strictly-increasing), DT1/2 grades monotone+in-range, DT3 tier map overlay→menu/floating→popover/content→content, DT4 zero-machinery no-blur-leak + deep-recipe-reads-depth — + its self-test teeth incl. the NEW DT4-FREEZE (`:root`-declared LERP flagged) + DT4-LADDER (flat blur ladder flagged) bites, all teeth ✓; `vue-tsc --noEmit` clean. PAINT rides W-REFLECT (menu vs popover vs button material thickness, both modes). **Prior state (SUPERSEDED):** PENDING (paint FAIL — fix owed per `docs/tranches/BG/audit/visual/BG.W-GLASS-DEPTH-TIER-DELTA.md`; src SHAs preserved: `glass-deep.css` 8bf3c4a2 / `glass/deep.css` ec048808) — **[JUDGED-FAIL 2026-07-05, dual-engine Chrome/Metal + WebKit/Metal, both modes]** the deep LERP is FROZEN at `:root`: `--glass-blur-deep-active-radius`/`--glass-saturate-deep-active` reference the REGISTERED `@property --glass-depth`, which CSS eager-substitutes at the `:root` declaration site with its `initial-value: 1`, so the LERP bakes `* 1` and inherits frozen — every deep surface paints FLAT 16px / saturate 1.8 regardless of tier grade (menu = popover = button; the live CTA at content-grade 0.35 paints 16px, not ~14px). The grade SCALAR resolves correctly per tier (overlay 1 / floating 0.7 / content 0.35) but is a DEAD KNOB on the paint — thickness-by-prominence does NOT paint. Fences held: calm default byte-unchanged, one-deep-per-route, no `--glass-blur-*` re-pointed. `proof:glass` DT4 green over broken (it text-checks the calc mentions `var(--glass-depth)` but never evaluates the freeze). — the tier-ladder depth MAP INTEGRATED on `tranche/BG`: the ONE inheriting `--glass-depth` scalar mapped onto the tier ladder with ZERO new machinery (three named per-band grade tokens `--glass-depth-content` 0.35 < `--glass-depth-popover` 0.7 < `--glass-depth-menu` 1 in `tokens/glass-deep.css`, and the `:where()` tier-map rules in `glass/deep.css` — overlay→menu, floating→popover, content-band→content — so a deep surface resolves menu > popover > button thickness by construction; content~14px < popover~15px < menu 16px). D5-SAFE: no tier rule reads `var(--glass-blur-deep)` or re-points a `--glass-blur-*` token (the map is a `--glass-depth` SCALAR default ONLY; the calm ladder never reads `--glass-depth`, so a NON-deep surface is byte-unchanged and `proof:glass-cal` stays GREEN by construction), the deep recipe still reads `var(--glass-depth)` (the grade is load-bearing, not a dead knob). `proof:glass` GREEN on the integrated tree incl. the new depth-tier arm (DT1/2 grades monotone+in-range, DT3 tier map overlay→menu/floating→popover/content→content, DT4 zero-machinery no-blur-leak + deep-recipe-reads-depth) + its 7 self-test teeth (DT1 missing-grade / DT2 flat+reversed / DT3 missing-map / DT4 blur-leak+dead-knob), `vue-tsc --noEmit` clean. PAINT rides W-REFLECT (menu vs popover vs button material thickness, both modes). | `proof:glass` depth-tier arm — the WWDC25 grammar (larger/more-prominent glass = thicker material by construction) mapped onto the EXISTING `--glass-depth` inheriting scalar with ZERO new machinery: the overlay/menu rungs default a HIGHER `--glass-depth` than the content rungs (menu > popover > button material thickness — deeper blur/lens/shadow), a control blooming into a menu GAINS depth as part of the morph; the calm content default is BYTE-UNCHANGED (the deep tier stays opt-in for content; only the overlay/menu rung DEFAULTS lift), one-deep-refractive-per-route budget held (`docs/tranches/BG/audit/sota-design/RECOVERED-LIQUID-ANIM-FINDINGS.md` [8]) | depth-by-prominence readback / menu vs popover vs button, both modes | F2.3 (DONE deep-glass tier) | zero-machinery token-default mapping |

rows.sourceText: **Verdict:** The demo storybook is structurally sound where the lens feared most: chassis adoption is strong (128/150 story files compose StoryPage/StorySection/Demo* directly; the 21 without are legitimate sub-components), interactive specimens render at natural width (the buttons/forms/select pages show no oversized full-width specimens — the 25 w-full uses are canvases, skeletons, auth CTAs, comboboxes), the landing bento renders distinct per-story Canvas2D stills (the D6 "11-identical-frozen-aurora" cure works), and no raw config/state debug dumps are rendered. The dominant defect mechanism is META-LANGUAGE LEAK VIA LIBRARY DATA: a grep of demo/stories reads clean of tranche/wave IDs in rendered text, yet the springs page RENDERS "BD.W-ANIM-IOS27-TUNE" verbatim because all six SPRING_PRESETS comment: fields (src/composables/motion/springPresets.ts) carry the wave name + engine jargon and springs.vue:191 binds {{ presetRow.comment }} — and those strings SHIP in the published dist bundle. Beyond that, ~10-15 motion/dock/substrate blurbs are written in engineering voice (keyframes.js internals ElementMorph/springTimingFunction/springLinearStops named, sibling libs named, "PRM" unglossed shorthand) directly against the "no meta on any demo page" mandate. Code blocks are standardized onto ONE CodeBlock primitive but have ZERO syntax highlighting (both sibling repos use highlight.js ^11.11.1 with a house .hljs theme) and CodeBlock is adopted on only 1 page while 2 pages hand-roll raw <pre>. Source-comment meta pollution is pervasive (~179 tranche.W- refs; nearly every demo file carries one) — source-only, but a repo-cleanliness miss for a 5.0.0 "disciplined not dirty" cut. Worst pages: springs, curve-gallery, glass-material, cta-receive, constellation, reveal, card-pressable.
